subject: Pricing band rebalancing & proposed exhibit language — please advise
messages:
From: Sven Hoffmann <sven.hoffmann@novaforge.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@novaforge.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rebalancing the pricing bands — request for clearer floor mechanics

Laura —

Thanks for the draft order form. Our procurement and finance teams ran the schedule against projected Q3 usage and flagged a concern: the proposed band rebalancing language could push committed minimum payouts above our forecast if usage drops slightly. Specifically, Section 2.c (Band Rebalance) and Exhibit B (Fee Floors) are ambiguous around how leftover commit credits are amortized.

Could you confirm whether the floor floors are evaluated monthly or quarterly, and whether there is an automatic prorate/true-up on termination? We want to avoid a situation where an early true-up results in a lump-sum invoice that exceeds our quarterly cash plan.

Attached: Exhibit-B_pricing_playbook_v2.pdf (for reference).

Best,
Sven
Head of Procurement, Novaforge

---
Attachment: Exhibit-B_pricing_playbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sven Hoffmann <sven.hoffmann@novaforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rebalancing the pricing bands — request for clearer floor mechanics

Sven —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answers up front: 1) Floors are evaluated on a quarterly basis for billing (quarterly true-up), 2) on termination we do a final quarterly true-up pro rata to the termination date (not a separate accelerated lump-sum), and 3) leftover credits are carried forward only within the contract year, subject to Exhibit B caps.

I’m attaching a short suggested edit to Exhibit B that: (a) clarifies quarterly evaluation windows, (b) adds an explicit pro rata termination true-up example, and (c) caps retained credits at 12% of the quarterly committed spend so we avoid runaway carryovers. Proposed language is intentionally prescriptive to reduce ambiguity for both sides.

If that works for you, I can have Legal (cc’d) produce a redline for your counsel.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm the carry-forward cap number (12% above) or propose an alternative.
- If accepted, we’ll circulate a redline and aim to finalize prior to signature.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: OrderForm_NOV-2027-0421_draft.docx (Word, 85 KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Rebalancing the pricing bands — proposed redline

Folks —

Attaching a redline to Exhibit B with two variant options: Option A (conservative) keeps a fixed 12% carry cap and quarterly true-ups; Option B (customer-friendly) reduces the carry cap to 6% but adds a 30-day remediation window before a true-up invoice posts. I highlighted the language where we can be flexible vs. where we need to preserve minimum economics (burst credits + quantization surcharge).

My note to legal: keep the termination mechanics simple — prorate to the day and then apply the quarterly true-up calculation, do not accelerate remaining committed amounts beyond the contract year.

Attaching: Exhibit-B_pricing_playbook_v2_redline.pdf

- Karthik
General Counsel (contracts), Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Exhibit-B_pricing_playbook_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 310 KB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sven Hoffmann <sven.hoffmann@novaforge.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@novaforge.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rebalancing the pricing bands — commercial proposal

Sven / Anita —

Appreciate the prompt review. To bridge quickly: we can accept Option B (6% carry cap + 30-day remediation) with the understanding that if Novaforge requests a retroactive increase to committed volumes after remediation, the updated commit will be prospective only. In return, Redwood will offer a one-time 5% implementation credit applied to Q1 invoices post-commit signature (applies against committed tokens only).

Please confirm both items and we’ll convert the redline into final language and circulate for signature. If your team prefers Option A instead, we’d need to preserve a higher minimum commit for the first two quarters of the contract (this is a material economics point).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

---
Quick ask: can we get Novaforge to confirm by EOD Friday so procurement can feed finance?
From: Sven Hoffmann <sven.hoffmann@novaforge.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@novaforge.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rebalancing the pricing bands — commercial proposal

Marissa / Laura —

We reviewed Option B with our CFO and legal. We are willing to accept the 6% carry cap and 30-day remediation window provided the implementation credit is applied as you described and the contract includes the explicit quarterly proration example. Anita will attach a brief note with final markups; she has asked that the redline reflect the credit as an invoice-level credit and not a reduction to committed volume (so audit trail is clear).

Assuming the redline matches, we can sign next week. Thank you for being flexible.

Best,
Sven
